description: DUT accepts a TCP packet with Reserved field set to zero (RFC 793 §3.1, RFC 4413 §4.2.3)
approach:
[Objective]
The Reserved field is officially zero. RFC 793 §3.1 / RFC 4413 §4.2.3 require senders to set 0 and receivers to accept. This is the positive baseline — HEADER_06 covers nonzero (also accepted, ignored).

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester ⇄ DUT: handshake.
2. Tester → DUT: data with Reserved=0.
3. Observation: DUT acks with correct ack_num.

[Pass condition]
DUT acks the data normally.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_handshake_ack — handshake never completed
• Fail_no_data_ack — DUT did not ack data
• Fail_wrong_ack_num — ACK does not cover payload

verdicts.Fail_no_data_ack: No DUT ACK to reserved-zero data
verdicts.Fail_wrong_ack_num: DUT ack_num does not acknowledge payload
